inputs.f_string:
Analyze this video shot for reference-to-video generation. The frames are numbered and timestamped in chronological order - use the timestamps to reconstruct the motion precisely.

Respond in exactly two sections, in this exact format (do not include the ``` markers in your answer):

```
summary:
Scene description

detailed_description:
Action description
```

First section (summary - scene only, 2-3 sentences):
- environment and background: location type, key objects and their rough positions
- camera framing (close-up / medium / wide), camera angle (eye-level / high / low), and camera movement (static / pan / tilt / tracking / handheld)
- lighting: main light direction, day or night, bright or dim

Second section (detailed_description - actions only; this is the most important part, be exhaustive and precise):
- Reconstruct the whole action as a chronological timeline. For each phase give its approximate time range from the frame timestamps, e.g. "0.0-2.0s: ...", "2.0-4.5s: ...". Cover the entire clip from the first to the last frame, do not skip phases.
- For every movement state WHICH body part moves (head, shoulders, chest, waist, hips, arms, hands, legs), its DIRECTION (up/down, left/right, forward/backward, toward/away from the camera, clockwise/counter-clockwise), its AMPLITUDE (slight / moderate / large) and its SPEED (slow / medium / fast).
- If a movement repeats or loops, say so explicitly and estimate how many repetitions.
- State <Subject 1>'s position in the frame (left / center / right, near / far) and body orientation relative to the camera (facing the camera / profile / back to the camera / three-quarter), and how this orientation changes over time.
- Describe posture at each phase: standing / sitting / kneeling / lying / leaning / bending, weight shifts, knee bends, back arch, head tilt.
- Describe what the hands do at each phase: where they are, what they touch (own body, an object, the other person), and how they move.
- MOUTH AND SPEECH (critical for lip-sync): describe <Subject 1>'s mouth movements with their exact timing - when the mouth opens and closes, when the lips are visibly articulating speech, when the mouth stays still, when it opens wide (laughing, shouting) - phase by phase with time ranges. The original audio (speech, voice and all sounds) is taken directly from this reference video, and these mouth timings are used to keep the lip-sync exact, so report them precisely. If <Subject 2> is visible, describe his mouth movements and timing the same way.
- Describe gaze direction (into the camera / away / down / at the other subject) and the moments when it changes.
- Describe interactions with objects and with <Subject 2> if visible: what touches what, when the contact starts and ends.
- Refer to the woman as <Subject 1>. Refer to the man or any other person as <Subject 2>, and only if they are actually visible.
- STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: describing how the subjects LOOK - no body shape, face, hair, skin, clothing, garment colors or accessories. Never mention what <Subject 1> or <Subject 2> is wearing (their appearance comes from a separate reference image and any appearance words here would corrupt the generation). Naming a body part as the thing that MOVES is allowed and required; describing its appearance is forbidden.
- Only observable facts. Never use "appears", "seems", "suggesting", "probably", "likely". Do not describe things that do not happen.
- Output nothing outside the two sections.

Very important hint: {a}

inputs.f_string:
Analyze this reference image for identity-preserving video generation.

Refer to the woman as <Subject 1>. Write at most two lines of dense text (no lists, no headings).
Include, in this order:
- subject type
- overall proportions and silhouette
- face shape, hair color / length / style, and defining facial features, if visible
- clothing: exact garment type and its EXACT color (e.g. "white bikini", never just "bikini"), materials, accessories, distinctive markings, and makeup if any
- any features that must remain identical in every video frame

Clothing color is critical: state the precise color of every garment explicitly and unambiguously - it must be reproduced exactly as in this image.
Do NOT describe skin tone or skin color. Do NOT describe the image background, camera angle, pose, lighting, composition, or action. Describe only the subject's stable appearance. Output nothing else.
